sections.label: The opening
sections.line: The book reviewed, fixed, and sent as patches
sections.para: While Dinis read the printed release candidate 2, six editors reviewed the same text chapter by chapter. They cut and reordered without inventing anything, the principles behind their fixes were written down, and the result went into a vault as seven patches: 74,666 words down to 64,351.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Two reviews, thirteen principles, seven patches
sections.para: Dinis read the printed copy while agents reviewed the text. The main problem is repetition; the point should come first. Seven patches, the seventh for what fell between the parts. The book is drawn as a graph for the back cover, and it all sits in a vault, because applying a patch is the decision.

sections.label: Reading it twice
sections.line: Reading the printed book, and asking for an editor
sections.para: Dinis is reading the 168 printed pages with a pen. He asked the agent to do an editor's work on the same text: propose and make changes, find the principles behind them, suggest pacing and structure, and bring over what works on the newsroom, including a picture of the book itself.

sections.label: Six editors and one rule
sections.line: Six editors in parallel, never inventing anything
sections.para: Each part went to its own editor, who read Dinis's voice and three recent articles first. They could cut, reorder, merge and rephrase; anything new became a question for Dinis. Every For Dinis note and quotation was kept, and each chapter and part got a note.

sections.label: What they found
sections.line: Repetition, a hidden point, pasted articles, no result
sections.para: The same stories appear in two to four chapters. The core idea first appeared in chapter 2's eighth paragraph. Chapter 11 was its article. Two titles named Dinis's products, now idea first and stake declared. And the company part has five chapters of argument and no result.

sections.label: The hands-on part
sections.line: Hands-on chapters instruct, and could be interleaved
sections.para: Chapter 30 was 49% chapter 13, and 39 was 37% chapter 19. Now each opens with what you will have, points back once, and gives the steps. Interleaving them, each at the end of the part it serves, fits the book's own rule: a manual, not a journey.

sections.label: What fell between the parts
sections.line: Two editors cut the same steps, each pointing away
sections.para: The editors of chapters 12 and 36 each cut the newsroom recipe and pointed to the other chapter, so the steps were in neither. A pass across the parts found it and four stale citations. Parallel work can be right in each lane and wrong as a whole.

sections.label: The principles
sections.line: Thirteen principles, starting with one home per story
sections.para: Each idea, story, quote and number lives in one chapter; pointers say what is there; a hand-off is checked on the other side. The point comes first and the story last. A chapter is not its article. Idea, example, stake. Co-writing is said on the first page.

sections.label: The book, drawn as itself
sections.line: The book as a graph, for the back cover
sections.para: The 41 chapters in a ring, sized by ideas and coloured by part, with lines where chapters share three or more sources. It shows the hands-on chapters barely joined to the argument, and it changes when the book does. Altitudes, versions and review records come from the newsroom too.

sections.label: Why a vault and not a pull request
sections.line: Patches in a vault keep the decision with Dinis
sections.para: The agent had no write access to the book's repository and did not need it. Seven patches, the patched chapters, the principles and 48 notes went into an encrypted sgit vault. Whoever applies a patch accepts it, and declining with a reason is an answer.

sections.label: What happens next
sections.line: Compare the pen marks, then answer the company questions
sections.para: Dinis will compare his marks on the printed copy with the patches; where they disagree, that is a finding about the review. Then come the seven answers only he has, starting with a company from registration to first payment.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A proposal, not applied, measured by the editors
sections.para: The review is an editor's reading until Dinis signs it off. The patches are unapplied, against v0.2.34, and the book's build was not run on them. The overlap figures are the editors'. The next release candidate has its own brief.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: A memo, a photo, and the book's source
sections.para: Dinis's voice memo and photograph of 19 October 2026, release candidate 2 read in full at book site v0.2.34, the book team's zoom in article, and related newsroom articles, written up and checked by newsroom.writer.
